text:
Maeve (Finance): Hey team - QuotaForge invoice PF-3321 looks off. There's an 'overage smoothing' credit that doesn't match the CSV math. Can someone sanity-check? :eyes:

Maeve (Finance): Vendor summary: 
```
PO: PF-3321
Commit: $30,000/mo (100M tokens)
Reported usage: 118,600,000 tokens
They claim overage charge: $2,364
They applied smoothing credit: $1,200
Final due on invoice: $31,164
```

Jules (Procurement): Tagging @Owen @Nina. Do we know what SKU mapping they used? Per-token rounding could explain small diffs.

Owen (Platform): Their docs list transformer.tokens @ $0.00002/token and access.stream @ $50/mo per stream. If all 18.6M overage tokens billed at $0.00002 => $372. So the $2,364 number implies other adders or different per-token rate.

Nina (Billing): Pulled the line-level export they attached. CSV snippet: 
```
line_id,sku,units,unit_price,subtotal,credit_code,credit_amt
L001,transformer.tokens,118600000,0.00002,2372,,0
L002,commit_discount,100000000,-0.00001,-1000,,0
L003,overage_smoothing,18600000,0.000064,1190,CF-SMOOTH,1200
```
Note L003 subtotal 1190 vs credit_amt 1200 and unit_price 0.000064 doesn't give exactly that subtotal (18600000 * 0.000064 = 1190.4). They also applied CF-SMOOTH as a credit code but the credit_amt doesn't algebraically match lines.

Maeve (Finance): Right — contract says smoothing should never increase net billed amount vs raw calc. Here it's messy. Also rounding looks inconsistent (1190 vs 1190.4 vs 1200).

Iris (BillingBot): Invoice PF-3321 anomaly flagged. anomaly_score=0.87. Recommended: manual review + request vendor breakdown.

Jules (Procurement): I'll draft a clarification email: request per-SKU rates used, exact formula for CF-SMOOTH, sample calculation reproducing invoice, and a CSV with separate fields for credit code, credit amount, and per-line pre/post rounding. Will route to @Sam for legal wording.

Sam (Legal): Include a request for appendix-level sample calc in the contract renewal: require per-invoice parity of credits and a mutual rounding rule (e.g., round halves up at line subtotal, then round final total to cents). If they decline, propose a capped overage rate or a 6-month pilot on same terms.

Owen (Platform): If CF-SMOOTH depends on burst shape, happy to run a 7-day flattened-traffic simulation from our side and share the token/time series so they can show the smoothing step. Might expose the rounding behavior.

Nina (Billing): If vendor can't provide deterministic formula, our fallback is to reject the smoothing adjustment for automation and ask for raw true-up math on each invoice. That keeps our parser simple.

Maeve (Finance): Good. Jules, please include the PO number and ask for the native CSV export (not a PDF) and a machine-readable mapping of credit_code -> explanation. Also ask them to reissue a corrected invoice if math != reproducible.

Jules (Procurement): Draft ready. Will paste here for quick review and then send to billing@quota.forge + acctmgr. Expect send in ~45m. :thumbsup:

Nina (Billing): One more ask: request their timezone for invoice cut and any monthly prorate rules. We had a previous vendor with a mid-month cut that caused odd proration.

Maeve (Finance): Thanks. If they push on price instead of transparency, I'll prepare proposed fallback terms: blended commit + capped overage at $0.00005/token or a 10% discount on overage. Will share numbers after Jules posts email.

Iris (BillingBot): Note added to invoice record: follow_up_required=true, follow_up_by=Jules (Procurement), due=2098777200.
